papers.title: Probiotics and diarrhoea morbidity among infants in Tanzania: secondary analysis of a randomised clinical trial.
papers.abstract: Diarrhoea causes annually more than 444 000 deaths in children globally, the majority in infants in low-income countries. The gut microbiota is a key determinant in resilience against enteric infections. We evaluated the effects of Bifidobacterium-based probiotic supplementation on diarrhoea morbidity among infants in Tanzania and explored associations between the gut microbiota composition at 6 weeks of age and later diarrhoeal risk.
papers.summary: This secondary analysis of a randomized clinical trial in Tanzania examined whether Bifidobacterium-based probiotic supplementation reduces diarrhoea in infants, and whether gut microbiota composition at 6 weeks predicts later diarrhoeal risk. The study links early-life microbiome features to enteric infection resilience in a low-income setting.

papers.title: CAnDi: a global catalogue of anaerobic digestion microbiomes.
papers.abstract: Methanogenic environments harbour complex prokaryotic consortia that drive the anaerobic conversion of organic matter into methane and carbon dioxide. Beyond being key to the global carbon cycle, such processes have been steered into powerful biotechnologies for energy production in bioreactors. Decoding the functional and taxonomic landscape of these communities requires comprehensive surveys, including bacteriophages and plasmids, which, however, remain vastly underrepresented in current databases. Here, we present the microbial Catalogue of Anaerobic Digestion (CAnDi), a database comprising
papers.summary: CAnDi is a new global database cataloguing the microbiomes of anaerobic digestion, the microbial communities that convert organic matter into methane and carbon dioxide. It compiles comprehensive taxonomic and functional surveys of these methanogenic consortia, including understudied components like bacteriophages and plasmids. This resource aims to support both understanding of the global carbon cycle and engineering of bioreactors for energy production.

papers.title: Influence of Gliricidia sepium living support on rhizosphere bacterial recruitment and fruit metabolomics in black pepper (Piper nigrum).
papers.abstract: The ability of the rhizosphere to recruit beneficial microorganisms is central to the sustainable management of crops. Here, we investigated, through shotgun metagenomic sequencing and mass spectrometry techniques, the microbial composition, antimicrobial resistance (AMRs), and metabolomic profiles of Piper nigrum cultivated under two support systems: living Gliricidia sepium support (SL/RL) and dead wooden support (SD/RD). Bulk and rhizosphere soils were sequenced to assess taxonomic structure and ARGs, with emphasis on Actinobacteria due to their relevance in antibiotic production. Actinobac
papers.summary: This study compared black pepper plants grown with living Gliricidia sepium support trees versus dead wooden supports, using shotgun metagenomics and mass spectrometry to profile rhizosphere bacteria and fruit metabolites. Living support altered rhizosphere bacterial recruitment, including Actinobacteria and antimicrobial resistance genes, and was associated with distinct fruit metabolomic profiles. The work suggests that living support systems can shape beneficial microbial recruitment and crop chemistry in a sustainable agricultural context.

papers.title: Senimuribacter muris sp. nov., a butyrate-producing bacterium isolated from mouse feces, and reclassification of members of the family Eubacteriaceae into the family Anaerovoracaceae.
papers.abstract: Two strictly anaerobic, Gram-stain-positive, non-motile, and rod-shaped bacterial strains, designated rT4E-8T and mB4P-1, were isolated from the feces of specific-pathogen-free Mus musculus (C57BL/6J). Both strains were catalase- and oxidase-negative and produced butyrate as a major fermentation product, with optimal growth at 37 °C and pH 7. The two strains shared 100% pairwise 16S rRNA gene sequence similarity and showed high similarity to Senimuribacter intestinalis DSM 106208T (95.1-95.3%). Genome sizes of strains rT4E-8T and mB4P-1 were 2.9 Mbp and 2.8 Mbp, with genomic DNA G+C contents o
papers.summary: The authors describe two new anaerobic, butyrate-producing bacterial strains isolated from mouse feces, which they propose as a novel species, Senimuribacter muris. They also propose reclassifying members of the family Eubacteriaceae into the family Anaerovoracaceae based on phylogenetic evidence. This work expands the known diversity of gut bacteria in laboratory mice and revises taxonomy of a broader bacterial group.

papers.title: Microbiology Galaxy Lab: a community-driven gateway for reproducible and FAIR analysis of microbiological data.
papers.abstract: The explosion of microbial omics data has outpaced the ability of many researchers to analyse it, with complex tools and limited computational resources creating barriers to discovery. To address this gap, we present the Microbiology Galaxy Lab (MGL): a free, globally accessible, community-supported platform that combines state-of-the-art analytical power with user-friendly accessibility. Supported by the Galaxy and global microbiology communities, this platform integrates over 315 tool suites and 115 curated workflows, enabling comprehensive metabarcoding, (meta)genomic, (meta)transcriptomic,
papers.summary: The authors present the Microbiology Galaxy Lab, a free, community-supported web platform that bundles over 315 tool suites and 115 curated workflows for reproducible analysis of microbial omics data. It aims to lower computational and technical barriers for microbiologists by providing accessible, FAIR-compliant pipelines for metabarcoding, metagenomics, and metatranscriptomics. The platform is backed by the Galaxy ecosystem and global microbiology communities.

papers.title: From saccharides to methane: substrate-driven microbial diversity and methanogenesis in anaerobic digestion revealed by 390 MAGs.
papers.abstract: Anaerobic digestion (AD) is a key technology for organic waste treatment and renewable energy production, yet its microbial processes remain poorly understood. This study employed genome-centric metagenomics to investigate synthetic AD systems fed with five substrates: starch, glucose, butyrate, propionate-valerate, and acetate. A total of 390 high-quality metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) were reconstructed, 64.36% of which represent potentially novel species. Substrate-driven selection shaped distinct functional consortia, with Bifidobacterium enriched in starch hydrolysis and Syntrophomon
papers.summary: This study reconstructed 390 high-quality metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) from synthetic anaerobic digestion systems fed with five different substrates, revealing that substrate type strongly selects for distinct microbial consortia and functional pathways. Nearly two-thirds of the MAGs represent potentially novel species, substantially expanding the known genomic diversity of anaerobic digestion microbiomes. The work provides a genome-resolved framework linking substrate chemistry to methanogenesis and microbial community assembly.

papers.title: Taxonova: Deep learning enables fast and confidence-aware microbiome species-level amplicon classification.
papers.abstract: Accurate species-level taxonomic classification of microbial amplicon sequences remains challenging due to the difficulty of resolving subtle variations within conserved ribosomal regions. Traditional similarity-based methods struggle with short amplicons and sequences with poor database representation. No existing method performs robustly across the full spectrum of amplicon lengths, limiting applicability across diverse sequencing platforms and variable-region targets. We present Taxonova, a deep learning framework for both short- and long-read ribosomal amplicons. Evaluated across physical
papers.summary: Taxonova is a deep learning framework for species-level taxonomic classification of microbial amplicon sequences that works across both short- and long-read platforms. It addresses the limitations of similarity-based methods, which struggle with short amplicons and poorly represented taxa, by providing confidence-aware predictions. The tool aims to be robust across diverse amplicon lengths and variable-region targets.

papers.title: Microbiome science needs AI competence, not just AI literacy.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence is rapidly becoming embedded in microbiome research, yet the way microbiome scientists are trained has not kept pace. Existing discussions frequently emphasize AI literacy and responsible tool use. We argue that literacy alone is insufficient in a field where data leakage, incomplete metadata, ecological confounding, inappropriate model selection and unverified generative-AI outputs can produce convincing but biologically misleading conclusions. We propose an AI-competence framework comprising five connected capabilities: data and platform fluency, machine-learning comp
papers.summary: The authors argue that microbiome researchers need deeper AI competence rather than basic AI literacy, because common pitfalls like data leakage, incomplete metadata, ecological confounding, and unverified generative-AI outputs can yield convincing but biologically misleading results. They propose a five-part AI-competence framework covering data and platform fluency, machine-learning competency, and related capabilities to guide training in the field.

papers.title: Early-life bovine respiratory virome analysis reveals phage-driven adaptation and cross-host evolutionary signatures.
papers.abstract: Past outbreaks of zoonotic viral infections highlight the importance of understanding respiratory virome ecology. As major food-producing animals with frequent human contact, cattle represent a critical host at the human-animal interface; however, the early-life establishment of their respiratory virome and its evolutionary connections to viruses from other hosts remain underexplored. Here, we longitudinally profile the upper respiratory tract (URT) virome of beef calves from birth to weaning using an optimized viral enrichment procedure and metagenomic workflow. Viral communities exhibited in
papers.summary: This study longitudinally profiles the upper respiratory tract virome of beef calves from birth to weaning, revealing that viral communities are dynamic and include phage-driven adaptation. The findings highlight cross-host evolutionary signatures, suggesting that the calf respiratory virome is shaped by interactions with phages and viruses from other hosts, with implications for understanding zoonotic risks at the human-animal interface.

papers.title: Microencapsulated immunoglobulin Y and lactic acid bacteria improve intestinal health in Yanbian Yellow calves.
papers.abstract: Neonatal calf diarrhea remains a major cause of morbidity and growth impairment, highlighting the need for stable and effective antibiotic alternatives that can simultaneously suppress enteric pathogens and improve gut health. We aimed to develop microcapsules containing immunoglobulin Y (IgY) and mixed lactic acid bacteria (LAB), termed IgY-LAB-MCs, and to evaluate their efficacy and optimal dosage as an alternative strategy for preventing calf diarrhea.
papers.summary: This study developed microcapsules containing immunoglobulin Y (IgY) and mixed lactic acid bacteria (IgY-LAB-MCs) as an antibiotic alternative to prevent neonatal calf diarrhea. The researchers evaluated the efficacy and optimal dosage of these microcapsules in Yanbian Yellow calves, finding that they improved intestinal health by suppressing enteric pathogens and enhancing gut health.

papers.title: Nutrient control enables metabolic reconstruction of Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus GG and analysis of secretions.
papers.abstract: Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus GG (LGG) is an important gut commensal bacterial strain that has been extensively studied in both industrial and health settings. Despite its long history of study, a high-quality genome-scale metabolic network model (GEM) for LGG has yet to be reconstructed. Only automatically generated draft models have been published, which have notoriously limited functional accuracy. Furthermore, comprehensive nutrient requirements have not been established for well-controlled in vitro studies. Here, we present the first curated GEM for LGG using a new approach for reconstruct
papers.summary: The authors present the first manually curated genome-scale metabolic model for the probiotic strain Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus GG, addressing the lack of a high-quality model beyond automatically generated drafts. They also establish comprehensive nutrient requirements for controlled in vitro growth and use the model to analyze secreted metabolites. This provides a more accurate framework for studying LGG metabolism in industrial and gut contexts.

papers.title: Hospital Drain Microbiomes as Distinct Microbial Signatures Within Urban Wastewater Networks in the Han River Watershed.
papers.abstract: Background: Hospital drainage systems represent an important interface between healthcare facilities and urban wastewater networks and may contribute distinct microbial inputs to downstream aquatic environments. This issue is particularly relevant in Seoul, Republic of Korea, where urban wastewater discharges into receiving waters within the Han River watershed. Methods: In this study, we characterized hospital drain microbiomes to evaluate their microbial and environmental signatures, using residential drains as a non-clinical comparison. Results: Hospital drains exhibited a distinct taxonomi
papers.summary: This study compared the microbiomes of hospital drains to residential drains within Seoul's urban wastewater network, finding that hospital drains harbor distinct taxonomic signatures. These findings suggest healthcare facilities contribute unique microbial inputs to urban wastewater that could be tracked downstream in the Han River watershed.

papers.title: Machine Learning in Mammals' Health: Integrating Multi-Omics Data for Precision Nutrition and Sustainable Production.
papers.abstract: Precision nutrition in modern mammalian production aims to transition from static feeding regimens toward dynamic and customized strategies by unraveling complex interactions among genetics, environment, the gut microbiome, and host physiology. Machine learning provides a powerful analytical framework to navigate high-dimensional multi-omics datasets. However, existing applications frequently lack systematic criteria for algorithm selection and remain largely confined to observational statistical associations without progressing toward causal verification. This perspective delineates a coheren
papers.summary: This perspective article argues that precision nutrition for mammalian livestock production can be advanced by integrating multi-omics data (genetics, microbiome, physiology) through machine learning, moving beyond static feeding regimens toward dynamic, customized strategies. The authors highlight a key gap: current ML applications often lack systematic criteria for algorithm selection and remain limited to observational associations rather than causal verification. The paper proposes a coherent framework for combining multi-omics data with ML to support precision nutrition and sustainable production.

papers.title: Shenqi Granules Ameliorate Cerebral Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury by Regulating Glucocerebrosidase and Uridine Metabolism in Microglia.
papers.abstract: Objective: Shenqi Granules is a traditional Chinese medicine formula derived from the classic prescription Shenqi Formula (SQF), composed of Astragali Radix (Huangqi) and Codonopsis Radix (Dangshen). SQF shows neuroprotection in cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI), but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Methods: The rat model of middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) was established using the suture method to evaluate the neuroprotective effect of SQF. Blood-absorbed components were identified via UHPLC-Q-TOF-MS/MS, and potential targets and pathways were predicted through netw
papers.summary: This study shows that Shenqi Granules, a traditional Chinese medicine formula, protect against cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury in rats by acting on microglia. Using network pharmacology and metabolomics, the authors link the protective effect to regulation of glucocerebrosidase and uridine metabolism in microglia.

papers.title: Continuous Glucose Monitoring for Metabolic Phenotyping and Precision Nutrition: Current Evidence, Clinical Applications and Future Perspectives.
papers.abstract: Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) has evolved beyond conventional diabetes management into an enabling technology for metabolic phenotyping and precision nutrition by providing continuous, real-world assessment of individual glycemic responses to dietary and lifestyle exposures. This narrative review examines the principles and clinical utility of CGM and its emerging applications in metabolic monitoring and personalized nutrition, with particular emphasis on postprandial glycemic variability, computational prediction, dietary feedback, and behavioral interventions. A literature search was c
papers.summary: This narrative review examines how continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) has expanded beyond diabetes care into metabolic phenotyping and precision nutrition, focusing on postprandial glycemic variability, computational prediction of glucose responses, and dietary feedback interventions. It synthesizes current evidence on CGM's clinical utility and discusses behavioral interventions and future directions for personalized nutrition.

papers.title: Next-Generation Functional Nanoplatforms: Engineering Plant-Derived Extracellular Vesicles for Targeted Bioactive Delivery and Health Applications.
papers.abstract: Plant-derived extracellular vesicles (PDEVs) are being recognized as a capable novel class of natural nanocarriers that have important uses in delivering bioactives and facilitating innovations in functional foods and precision health technologies. PDEVs are lipid-bilayer-enclosed vesicular structures that commonly occur at the nanoscale, although their reported sizes vary depending on the plant source, isolation procedure, and measurement method. They contain diverse biomolecules, including lipids, proteins, microRNAs, and phytochemicals, and have been investigated for their potential roles i
papers.summary: This review examines plant-derived extracellular vesicles (PDEVs) as natural nanocarriers for delivering bioactive compounds, highlighting their lipid-bilayer structure and cargo of lipids, proteins, microRNAs, and phytochemicals. It discusses how PDEV size and composition vary by plant source and isolation method, and surveys their potential applications in functional foods and precision health technologies.

papers.title: Multikingdom and functional gut microbiota markers for cholangiocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: While the association between gut microbiota and cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) has been explored, existing research has been limited to bacterial components. The alterations in non-bacterial members (fungi, archaea, and viruses) and their functional characteristics in CCA remain unclear. This study aimed to comprehensively characterize the multi-kingdom gut microbiota and functional profiles in CCA patients and develop a non-invasive diagnostic model.
papers.summary: This study moves beyond bacteria to profile fungi, archaea, and viruses in the gut microbiome of cholangiocarcinoma patients, aiming to characterize multi-kingdom and functional alterations. The authors use these profiles to build a non-invasive diagnostic model for CCA. It extends prior bacterial-only microbiome studies of this cancer to a broader multi-kingdom and functional view.

papers.title: Identification of Genes Associated with Gut Microbiota Metabolites in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Complicated by Acute Cerebral Infarction Based on Bioinformatics and Mendelian Randomization.
papers.abstract: Background: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and acute cerebral infarction (ACI) are globally prevalent diseases that impose substantial public health burdens. While gut microbiota (GM) is increasingly recognized to regulate metabolic and immune homeostasis linked to both diseases, its shared genetically predicted microbial taxa and underlying metabolite-gene regulatory mechanisms in T2DM and ACI remain unclear, highlighting the need for systematic investigation. Accordingly, this study aimed to elucidate their regulatory mechanisms. Methods: Transcriptomic datasets, genome-wide association stu
papers.summary: This study integrates transcriptomic data with Mendelian randomization to identify gut microbiota taxa and metabolites that may be causally linked to type 2 diabetes complicated by acute cerebral infarction, and to nominate genes mediating these metabolite-gene regulatory relationships. It proposes shared microbial and metabolic pathways underlying the two conditions, offering candidate biomarkers and mechanistic hypotheses for future validation.

papers.title: Exploratory Shotgun Metagenomic Analysis of the Fecal Microbiome and Antimicrobial-Resistance Potential in Simmental Calves with Different Diarrheal Statuses.
papers.abstract: Calf diarrhea is frequently accompanied by disruption of the gastrointestinal microbiota, but the relationships between clinical status and microbial community composition, gene-content functional potential, and antimicrobial-resistance-associated features remain incompletely characterized. This exploratory study aimed to characterize these features in calves with different diarrheal statuses using shotgun metagenomics. Six approximately 2-month-old Simmental calves from Chahar Right Middle Banner, Inner Mongolia, were included, comprising two healthy calves, two calves with mild diarrhea, and
papers.summary: This exploratory study used shotgun metagenomics to compare the fecal microbiome and antimicrobial-resistance gene potential of six Simmental calves grouped by diarrheal status (healthy, mild, and presumably more severe diarrhea). The small sample size limits statistical power, but the work characterizes compositional and functional differences associated with diarrhea in calves. It is a preliminary descriptive contribution rather than a definitive causal or diagnostic finding.

papers.title: Limited Gut Microbiome Differences Between Relapsing-Remitting and Secondary Progressive Multiple Sclerosis: A Shotgun Metagenomic Study.
papers.abstract: The gut microbiome may contribute to multiple sclerosis (MS) pathophysiology, but its relationship with disease phenotype and progression remains unclear. To characterize taxonomic and functional gut microbiome differences between relapsing-remitting MS (RRMS) and secondary progressive MS (SPMS) and their associations with neurological disability and circulating biomarkers. This cross-sectional study included 89 participants (30 healthy controls, 29 RRMS, and 30 SPMS). Shotgun metagenomic sequencing was used to assess microbial diversity, taxonomic profiles, and predefined short-chain fatty ac
papers.summary: This cross-sectional shotgun metagenomic study compared gut microbiome composition and function across 89 participants (30 healthy controls, 29 relapsing-remitting MS, and 30 secondary progressive MS). The authors found only limited taxonomic and functional differences between RRMS and SPMS, suggesting that gut microbiome signatures do not strongly distinguish these disease phenotypes. Associations with neurological disability and circulating biomarkers were modest, indicating the microbiome's role in MS progression may be less pronounced than hypothesized.

papers.title: From Microbiome Associations to Deployable Precision Probiotics in Animals: A Critical Narrative Review and Proposed Causal Evidence Framework for Next-Generation Probiotic Development.
papers.abstract: Next-generation probiotics (NGPs) are promoted as precision tools for animal health, yet the term is often applied to uncommon taxa before causality, safety and target-species efficacy are established. This critical narrative review reframes animal NGPs as a development pathway rather than a taxonomic category. A structured PubMed search was last run on 14 September 2026 with a publication date cutoff of 1 September 2026 and was supplemented by citation tracing and targeted searches of authoritative sources. From the screened literature, 45 representative and conceptually informative sources w
papers.journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
papers.summary: This critical narrative review argues that "next-generation probiotics" for animals should be defined as a development pathway rather than a taxonomic label, since many candidate taxa are promoted before causality, safety, and target-species efficacy are established. The authors synthesize 45 representative sources and propose a causal evidence framework to guide the progression from microbiome associations to deployable precision probiotics.

papers.title: Rethinking Solid-Phase Microextraction (SPME) for Bioanalysis: Workflow Optimisation in Automated Vacuum-Assisted Cooling SPME for Fatty Acid Monitoring in Faecal Waters.
papers.abstract: Short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) are key biomarkers of gut microbiota and intestinal health, yet their analysis is challenging due to high volatility, hydrophilicity, and the complexity of the faecal matrix. This study introduces a novel, green, and fully automated workflow for monitoring SCFAs in faecal water samples. It combines microwave-assisted derivatisation, vacuum-assisted cooling multiple solid-phase microextraction (Vac-HS-cooling-MSPME), and fast gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS). On-sample derivatisation with 2,3,4,5,6-pentafluorobenzyl bromide was optimised via design of
papers.summary: This study presents a fully automated, green analytical workflow for measuring short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) in faecal water, combining microwave-assisted derivatisation with vacuum-assisted cooling multiple solid-phase microextraction (Vac-HS-cooling-MSPME) and fast GC-MS. The method addresses the volatility, hydrophilicity, and matrix complexity challenges of SCFA analysis, with derivatisation conditions optimised via design of experiments. It offers a practical approach for monitoring gut microbiota-related biomarkers in stool samples.

papers.title: Network Pharmacology of Natural Products from Computational Prediction to Experimental Validation.
papers.abstract: Natural products are important sources of bioactive compounds, but their complex chemical composition and multi-target effects make their mechanisms difficult to investigate using conventional approaches. Network pharmacology provides a systems-level framework for integrating chemical, biological, and disease-related information to investigate these complex interactions. This review describes the network pharmacology workflow, from active-compound screening, ADMET evaluation and target prediction to network construction and pathway enrichment, and the complementary roles of molecular docking a
papers.summary: This review describes the network pharmacology workflow for studying natural products, covering active-compound screening, ADMET evaluation, target prediction, network construction, and pathway enrichment, along with complementary molecular docking and experimental validation. It provides a systems-level framework for investigating the multi-target mechanisms of complex natural product mixtures that are difficult to study with conventional approaches.

papers.title: Dynamics of Gut Microbial Community and Function in Growing Male Raccoon Dogs.
papers.abstract: Background: Raccoon dogs have short breeding cycles and strong adaptability, and their fur is economically valuable. Although the gut microbiota, a key regulator of animal health, has been extensively studied in livestock, its composition and function in raccoon dogs remain poorly understood. Methods: In this study, the gut microbiota structure and functional profiles of ten raccoon dogs were analyzed during their growth period, including 2 (M2), 3 (M3), 4 (M4), 6 (M6), and 8 (M8) months after birth. Results: Our findings revealed that the richness and diversity of the gut microbiota in growin
papers.journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
papers.summary: This study tracked the gut microbiota of ten male raccoon dogs across five time points (2, 3, 4, 6, and 8 months after birth), characterizing both community composition and functional profiles. The authors found that microbial richness and diversity changed over the growth period, providing a first look at how gut microbial communities develop in this species. The work is largely descriptive and specific to raccoon dogs, with limited immediate relevance beyond this system.

papers.title: Integrated Metagenomic and Metatranscriptomic Analysis Reveals Microbiome Differences Between Bisexual and Parthenogenetic Populations of Haemaphysalis longicornis.
papers.abstract: The tick Haemaphysalis longicornis is an important vector of human and animal pathogens in East Asia that comprises both bisexual (Bis) and parthenogenetic (Par) populations. While previous studies have documented differences between these reproductive groups in genome ploidy, host transcription, and vector capacity, it remains unclear whether reproductive strategy is accompanied by systematic divergence in the tick-associated microbiome, including microbial community composition, transcriptional activities, and functional outputs. Here, we profiled laboratory-maintained Bis and Par population
papers.summary: This study compared the microbiome of bisexual and parthenogenetic populations of the tick Haemaphysalis longicornis using integrated metagenomic and metatranscriptomic sequencing. The authors found systematic differences in microbial community composition and transcriptional activity between the two reproductive groups, suggesting that reproductive strategy is associated with divergence in the tick-associated microbiome. These differences may have implications for vector capacity and pathogen transmission.

papers.title: Traditional Food Use and Ethnomedicinal Contexts of Turnip (Brassica rapa L.): A Scoping Review of Composition, Food Processing, and Health-Related Evidence.
papers.abstract: Turnip (Brassica rapa L.) is widely cultivated for food and has documented ethnomedicinal uses. This scoping review mapped the international literature on turnip, with detailed synthesis focused on turnip materials associated with selected regional food and ethnomedicinal traditions in China. Searches covered seven bibliographic databases. The bibliographic map comprised 771 records, of which 397 were selected for detailed synthesis. Regional uses varied in plant part and preparation method. The clearest evidence concerned composition and processing: constituent profiles differed by provenance
papers.summary: This scoping review mapped 771 records on turnip (Brassica rapa), synthesizing 397 in detail, with a focus on regional food and ethnomedicinal traditions in China. The strongest evidence concerned composition and food processing, showing that constituent profiles vary by provenance and preparation method, while health-related evidence was less conclusive.

papers.title: Soil Microbiome Signatures Associated with Epidemiological Heterogeneity Across Natural Plague Foci in Inner Mongolia, China.
papers.abstract: Plague persistence relies on complex host-vector-environment interactions, yet the ecological contribution of soil microbiomes to natural foci remains poorly understood. We performed shotgun metagenomic sequencing of 143 soil samples across four distinct plague foci in Inner Mongolia, China, to characterize microbiome features associated with contrasting epidemiological states. Taxonomic, functional, and network analyses showed that the three active plague foci exhibited lower microbial diversity, simplified co-occurrence networks, and enrichment of specific taxa, particularly Streptomyces. Co
papers.summary: Shotgun metagenomic sequencing of 143 soil samples from four plague foci in Inner Mongolia revealed that active plague foci had lower microbial diversity, simpler co-occurrence networks, and enrichment of specific taxa such as Streptomyces compared with inactive foci. The findings suggest soil microbiome signatures may correlate with epidemiological states of natural plague foci.

papers.title: Elevated Level of Fannyhessea vaginae Correlated with Implantation Outcomes in Women undergoing in vitro fertilization Treatment.
papers.abstract: The vaginal microbiome plays a significant role in reproductive health. While maintaining a balanced vaginal microbiome is crucial for successful in vitro fertilization (IVF) outcomes, the specific bacteria associated with adverse outcomes may vary by region and are largely unknown. This study aims to investigate the bacterial profiles and their influence on embryo implantation, thereby supporting the development of microbiome-based therapies. One hundred women undergoing IVF provided vaginal swabs at three stages: oocyte retrieval, embryo transfer, and hCG pregnancy testing. An in-house 16S r
papers.summary: This study profiled the vaginal microbiome of 100 women undergoing IVF at three time points (oocyte retrieval, embryo transfer, and pregnancy testing) using 16S rRNA sequencing. Elevated levels of Fannyhessea vaginae were associated with poorer embryo implantation outcomes, suggesting this bacterium may serve as a marker or target for microbiome-based interventions to improve IVF success.

papers.title: Dietary Fibre in Pea Cotyledon Used as a Protein Source Provides Multidimensional Protection Against Colonic Protein Putrefaction.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Substitution of plant-based for animal-based protein sources has been recommended to reduce global non-communicable disease burdens, including colorectal cancer. Objective: The goal of this study was to determine possible ways that pea cotyledon may modulate hindgut concentrations of protein putrefaction products implicated in colorectal cancer by comparing diets based on casein, meat or pea cotyledon in a rat model. Method: Rats (n = 8 per treatment) were fed for 9 days on 18.6% protein diets containing casein, meat, or yellow split peas as sole protein sources. Faecal
papers.summary: In a rat feeding trial, replacing casein or meat protein with pea cotyledon as the sole protein source reduced hindgut markers of protein putrefaction, compounds linked to colorectal cancer risk. The authors attribute this protection to the fibre naturally present in pea cotyledon, suggesting plant protein sources may lower colon cancer risk through combined protein and fibre effects.

papers.title: Short-Term Simulated NH4+/NO3- Inputs Reorganize Soil Microbial Communities and Modify N-Cycling Functional Potential in Temperate Forests.
papers.abstract: Forest soil nitrogen (N) turnover and nitrous oxide (N2O) release are strongly influenced by atmospheric N deposition. Although the effects of individual inorganic N species on soil biogeochemistry are well documented, the consequences of changing their relative supply for N2O formation and the underlying microbial pathways remain less clear. We therefore examined soil N2O emissions, microbial communities, and N-transformation potential across a gradient of ammonium-to-nitrate (NH4+/NO3-) inputs in a temperate forest soil from Northeast China. Seven treatments covering NH4+/NO3- ratios from 1:
papers.summary: This study tested how different ratios of ammonium to nitrate inputs affect soil microbial communities and nitrogen cycling in a temperate forest soil from Northeast China. The authors found that shifting the NH4+/NO3- balance reorganizes microbial community composition and alters the functional potential for nitrogen transformations, with consequences for nitrous oxide emissions. The work highlights that the relative supply of inorganic nitrogen species, not just total deposition, shapes soil biogeochemistry.

papers.title: Intratumoral Bacterial Profiles, Bacterial Co-Detection Patterns, and Molecular Alterations in Colorectal Cancer and Colorectal Polyps: A Vietnamese Cohort Study.
papers.abstract: Intratumoral microbiota may contribute to colorectal cancer (CRC), but their relationships with bacterial co-occurrence, relative bacterial loads, and molecular alterations remain incompletely understood. This study characterized intratumoral bacterial profiles in CRC and colorectal polyps and examined their clinicopathological and molecular associations. A cross-sectional study included 149 patients with CRC and 109 patients with benign colorectal polyps. F. nucleatum, ETBF, A. muciniphila, and eae+E. coli were detected in formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded tissues using multiplex real-time PC
papers.summary: This cross-sectional Vietnamese cohort study profiled intratumoral bacteria (F. nucleatum, ETBF, A. muciniphila, eae+ E. coli) in FFPE tissues from 149 colorectal cancer patients and 109 patients with benign polyps, examining co-detection patterns and associations with clinicopathological and molecular features. It provides regional data on tumor-associated bacterial profiles and their links to molecular alterations in colorectal carcinogenesis.

papers.title: Synovial SLC1A5-Associated Amino Acid Metabolic Features in Knee Osteoarthritis: An Integrated Analysis of Synovial Transcriptomics, Fecal Metabolomics, and Gut Microbiota.
papers.abstract: Background: This exploratory study aimed to characterize amino acid related features in osteoarthritis (OA). Methods: We analyzed independent public synovial transcriptomic datasets and paired fecal metabolomics and 16S ribosomal RNA profiles from 20 patients with knee OA and 14 controls. Metabolite-sensing genes were intersected with nominally differential genes and prioritized using elastic net, support vector machine recursive feature elimination, and extreme gradient boosting. Results:SLC1A5 (solute carrier family 1 member 5) expression was lower in the discovery cohort GSE89408 (log2 fold
papers.summary: This exploratory study integrated public synovial transcriptomic data with paired fecal metabolomics and 16S rRNA profiles from 20 knee osteoarthritis patients and 14 controls to identify amino acid metabolic features. The solute carrier gene SLC1A5 emerged as a prioritized metabolite-sensing gene with lower expression in OA synovium, linking synovial amino acid metabolism to gut microbiota and fecal metabolite profiles. The findings are preliminary and based on small, exploratory cohorts.

papers.title: Bifidobacterium longum Depletion and Bile Acid Dysregulation in MASLD: Links to Hepatic TGR5-AMPK Signaling.
papers.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is the most common chronic liver disease worldwide. Although gut microbiota dysbiosis and aberrant bile acid metabolism are central to MASLD pathogenesis, the critical keystone species and precise molecular mechanisms remain elusive. Here, we performed an integrated analysis of 14 public 16S rRNA datasets (275 controls, 352 patients), combining multi-method differential abundance screening, machine learning, and network analysis to pinpoint MASLD-specific microbial signatures. We further validated the therapeutic potential of can
papers.summary: This study integrates 14 public 16S rRNA datasets to identify Bifidobacterium longum depletion as a key microbial signature in MASLD, alongside bile acid dysregulation. The authors link these changes to hepatic TGR5-AMPK signaling and suggest a therapeutic role for can (likely a compound or intervention) in restoring this axis.

papers.title: Microbiome-Related Amino-Acid Profiles of Liver and Muscle Tissues in Arbor Acres Broiler Chickens.
papers.abstract: The study, designed as a group-level integrative data analysis, included homogeneous datasets obtained from 24 Arbor Acres chicken groups. Quantitative amino-acid analysis in chicken tissues was carried out using the capillary electrophoresis method. Gut microbial community analysis was performed using 16S rRNA gene-sequencing technology on the Illumina MiSeq platform. Amino-acid analysis of liver samples revealed 10 Arg-high and 14 Arg-low chicken groups, while for thigh samples, the ratio of Arg-high and Arg-low groups was 18/6, respectively. The gut microbiomes of chickens with an Arg-high
papers.summary: This study profiled amino acids in liver and thigh muscle tissue from 24 groups of Arbor Acres broiler chickens and correlated these profiles with gut microbiome composition using 16S rRNA sequencing. Groups were classified as having high or low tissue arginine levels, and the authors linked these amino-acid patterns to differences in the gut microbial community. The work suggests that microbiome composition is associated with tissue amino-acid profiles in poultry.

papers.title: Next-Generation Sequencing in Practical Wildlife Disease Investigation: Metagenomic Insights into European Bison and Gazelle Mortality and Morbidity Events.
papers.abstract: Wildlife disease investigations require diagnostic methods capable of detecting diverse and previously unrecognized pathogens. Metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) was applied to samples from three Dorcas gazelles (Gazella dorcas osiris) affected by sudden mortality and four European bison (Bison bonasus) with respiratory disease or necrotic balanoposthitis (NBP). No dominant bacterial species was detected in gazelles. In European bison, respiratory disease was associated with Pasteurella multocida, whereas NBP samples were dominated by Porphyromonas levii and other anaerobes. Dorcas
papers.summary: This study applied metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) to investigate disease events in captive wildlife: sudden mortality in three Dorcas gazelles and respiratory disease or necrotic balanoposthitis in four European bison. No dominant bacterial pathogen was identified in the gazelles, while bison respiratory disease was linked to Pasteurella multocida and the genital lesions were dominated by Porphyromonas levii and other anaerobes. The work demonstrates that mNGS can provide actionable pathogen leads in wildlife diagnostic investigations where conventional culture may fail.

papers.title: Scaffold-level validation is needed for phage-host inference from metagenome-assembled genomes.
papers.abstract: Accurate phage-host prediction underpins ecological interpretation and experimental validation of uncultivated phages, yet most current approaches rely heavily on metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs). This reliance implicitly assumes that MAG-level quality metrics, such as completeness and contamination, ensure scaffold-level correctness. Here, we demonstrate that this assumption can be violated under particular challenging conditions. Tetranucleotide frequency (TNF) analyses reveal that CRISPR-associated regions often diverge compositionally from their host genomes, increasing the risk of misb
papers.summary: This paper challenges the common assumption that high-quality metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) guarantee reliable phage-host predictions. The authors show that CRISPR-associated regions can differ compositionally from their host genomes, which can lead to misassignment of phage-host links when inference is done at the MAG level. They argue that scaffold-level validation is needed to avoid such errors.

papers.title: Optimized Super-SILAC Normalization Enables Enhanced Profiling of Histone Post-Translational Modification Changes Associated with Microbiota and Acute Inflammation.
papers.abstract: The gut microbiota produces metabolites, such as short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) that modulate histone acylation and serve as precursors for non-acetyl acyl marks, representing a mechanism in host-microbiome epigenetic crosstalk. However, the reliable quantification of these low-abundance modifications in complex tissues remains challenging. Here, we established an optimized, non-acetyl histone acylation-focused super-SILAC strategy for profiling histone post-translational modifications (HPTM) in the gut epithelium. We generated a functionally optimized internal standard from heavy-labeled col
papers.summary: The authors developed an optimized super-SILAC internal standard specifically focused on non-acetyl histone acylation marks, enabling reliable quantification of low-abundance histone post-translational modifications in complex gut tissue. Applying this to gut epithelium, they profiled HPTM changes linked to microbiota and acute inflammation, illuminating host-microbiome epigenetic crosstalk via SCFA-derived acyl marks.

papers.title: Genome-resolved taxonomy, global distribution, and EPS potential of Zoogloea, the canonical floc-former in wastewater treatment systems.
papers.abstract: The bacterial genus Zoogloea is the fourth most abundant genus in wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) globally, where it plays key roles in floc formation and nutrient removal but can also contribute to viscous bulking when highly abundant. The taxonomic assignment of Zoogloea has historically been inconsistent, as several taxa were classified based on phenotypic characteristics and later reassigned to other families or orders. This has obscured both the identity and distribution of Zoogloea and hindered interpretation of its floc-forming mechanisms, which have been attributed to polysaccharid
papers.summary: This study uses genome-resolved taxonomy to clarify the classification of Zoogloea, the fourth most abundant bacterial genus in wastewater treatment plants globally, resolving historical inconsistencies in its taxonomic assignment. It maps the genus's global distribution and assesses its potential for producing extracellular polymeric substances (EPS), which underlie floc formation and can cause viscous bulking. The work provides a clearer framework for understanding Zoogloea's ecological roles and floc-forming mechanisms in WWTPs.

papers.title: Infective endocarditis due to a novel Gemella species revealed by metagenomic sequencing.
papers.abstract: Gemella species are rare causes of infective endocarditis, and accurate species identification can be challenging with routine diagnostic methods. We report infective endocarditis caused by a novel Gemella species, highlighting the diagnostic value of sequencing-based approaches for bacteria not registered in public databases and the risk of misclassification when novel species are not represented in reference databases.
papers.summary: This case report describes infective endocarditis caused by a previously uncharacterized Gemella species that was identified through metagenomic sequencing after routine diagnostic methods failed to provide accurate species-level identification. The case highlights both the diagnostic power of sequencing-based approaches for detecting novel pathogens absent from public reference databases and the risk of misclassification when such species are not represented.

papers.title: Benchmarking nanopore-based strategies for antimicrobial resistance prediction.
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) presents a pressing need to ensure that the right antimicrobials are used to target the right microbes at the right time. Ideally, the appropriate antimicrobial is selected after patient samples have been cultured and assessed with antimicrobial sensitivity testing (AST). However, the time needed for culture-based diagnosis leads to immediate empirical treatment, often with broad-spectrum and/or high-tier antimicrobials. Direct nanopore metagenomic whole-genome sequencing to identify pathogens and predict their AMR is a rapid and patient-side alternative. A limit
papers.summary: This study benchmarks different nanopore sequencing strategies for predicting antimicrobial resistance directly from patient samples, aiming to bypass culture-based diagnostics that delay targeted treatment. It evaluates how well direct nanopore metagenomic whole-genome sequencing can identify pathogens and their resistance profiles compared to standard methods. The work provides guidance on which nanopore-based approaches are most reliable for rapid, patient-side AMR prediction.

papers.title: Seasonal and Environmental Influences on Microbial Community Dynamics in the Dunk River Watershed, Prince Edward Island, Canada.
papers.abstract: Riverine ecosystems are crucial biogeochemical hubs, with their microbial communities playing a key role in nutrient cycling and overall ecosystem health. This study used shotgun metagenomic sequencing to characterize the seasonal and environmental drivers of taxonomic and functional microbial community structure (read depth between 1.91 and 30.44 bp) in four tributaries of the Dunk River watershed in Prince Edward Island (PEI), a landscape shaped by intensive agriculture and groundwater-dominated streamflow, where the seasonal and land-use impacts on the river's microbiome remain understudied
papers.summary: This study used shotgun metagenomic sequencing to characterize how seasonal changes and environmental factors shape the taxonomic and functional composition of microbial communities in four tributaries of the Dunk River watershed in Prince Edward Island, a region dominated by intensive agriculture and groundwater-fed streams. The work provides a baseline characterization of riverine microbiome dynamics in an understudied agricultural landscape, linking land use and seasonality to microbial community structure.

papers.title: Cross hybridization inference for phylogenetic resolution-fluorescence in situ hybridization enables microbiome imaging with strain level taxonomic resolution.
papers.abstract: The spatial organization of microbial communities is a critical determinant of host-microbe interactions, yet species-level mapping remains challenging due to high 16S rRNA sequence homology and spectral crosstalk in multiplexed fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH). To address this challenge, we developed Cross-hybridization Inference for Phylogenetic Resolution (CIPHR)-FISH, a pipeline that integrates strategic probe design with supervised machine learning. CIPHR-FISH transforms probe cross-hybridization, traditionally viewed as experimental noise, into informative molecular signatures.
papers.summary: The authors present CIPHR-FISH, a pipeline that combines strategic probe design with supervised machine learning to turn probe cross-hybridization—normally treated as noise—into informative signatures for multiplexed fluorescence in situ hybridization. This enables spatial imaging of microbiomes at strain-level taxonomic resolution despite high 16S rRNA homology and spectral crosstalk.

papers.title: Human milk oligosaccharides are distinctly processed by early life gut microbial sialidases.
papers.abstract: The infant gut microbiome in early life is shaped by numerous factors, including feeding method. Exclusively breastfed and formula-fed infants exhibit distinct microbiome compositions. While these effects are well-established, the underlying mechanisms that drive these differences are not fully understood. Here, we examine the removal of sialic acid from human milk oligosaccharides (HMOs) influenced by human microbial sialidases in early life. We identify 351 and 214 unique sialidase sequences from adult and infant microbiome metagenomes, respectively, and characterize a diverse, representativ
papers.summary: This study identifies and characterizes sialidase enzymes from early-life gut microbiomes that remove sialic acid from human milk oligosaccharides (HMOs), revealing how infant gut microbes process these breast milk components differently from adult microbes. The researchers found 351 sialidase sequences in adult metagenomes versus 214 in infant metagenomes, and characterized a diverse set of representative enzymes. These findings help explain the mechanistic basis for microbiome differences between breastfed and formula-fed infants.

papers.title: Metagenomic analysis of tomato rhizosphere microbiomes detects Ralstonia phage sequences in Kenyan agricultural soils.
papers.abstract: Bacterial wilt caused by Ralstonia solanacearum species complex is a major constraint in tomato production in Kenya, resulting in yield losses of up to 100% in heavily infested fields. This study used high-throughput shotgun metagenomic sequencing approach to characterize the rhizosphere microbiomes of tomato plants in three of the major production areas in Kenya (Kirinyaga, Kiambu, and Laikipia counties) focusing on detecting Ralstonia phage sequences. Soil samples were collected from the rhizosphere of bacterial wilt-infected tomato plants, and microbial DNA was extracted using a modified ph
papers.summary: This study used shotgun metagenomic sequencing to characterize tomato rhizosphere microbiomes from three major tomato-growing counties in Kenya, with a focus on detecting Ralstonia phage sequences in bacterial wilt-infested soils. The work demonstrates that phage sequences associated with the Ralstonia solanacearum species complex can be detected in agricultural soils, providing a baseline for exploring phage-based biocontrol strategies against this devastating plant pathogen.

papers.title: A systematic review of the effects of diet on the gut microbiota in individuals at elevated risk for colorectal cancer.
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) poses a major public health concern, with emerging evidence highlighting the critical role of the gut microbiota in CRC progression. Considering that diet is a major modifiable factor influencing CRC risk, partly through its interaction with the gut microbiome, this systematic review evaluated the effects of dietary intervention RCTs, including supplements, functional foods, whole foods, and dietary patterns, on the gut microbiome in elevated-risk individuals.
papers.summary: This systematic review examines randomized controlled trials of dietary interventions—including supplements, functional foods, whole foods, and overall dietary patterns—and their effects on the gut microbiome in people at elevated risk for colorectal cancer. It synthesizes evidence on whether diet-driven microbiome changes could serve as a modifiable pathway for CRC risk reduction in high-risk populations.

papers.title: Co-occurrence and genetic contexts of NDM-1, KPC-2, IMP-1, and AFM-1 carbapenemase genes in a critically ill patient.
papers.abstract: Carbapenem-resistant organisms are increasingly reported in clinical settings, yet the simultaneous detection of multiple carbapenemase genes within a single specimen remains rare.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This report describes a critically ill patient in whom four distinct carbapenemase genes (NDM-1, KPC-2, IMP-1, and AFM-1) were detected simultaneously, an unusually rare co-occurrence. The authors characterize the genetic contexts and co-occurrence patterns of these resistance determinants, highlighting the potential for multi-carbapenemase carriage in clinical settings.

papers.title: Why does apical periodontitis persist? A shotgun metagenomic survey of the microbial community in primary and persistent periapical granulomas.
papers.abstract: This cross‑sectional observational study used shotgun metagenomic sequencing to compare the microbiomes of periapical granulomas from primary and persistent apical periodontitis to identify microbial taxa and functional pathways associated with persistent lesions.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study used shotgun metagenomic sequencing to compare the microbial communities in periapical granulomas from primary versus persistent apical periodontitis. The authors aimed to identify specific microbial taxa and functional pathways that distinguish persistent lesions, potentially explaining why some infections fail to resolve after treatment.

papers.title: A Two-Stage ESM-Based Machine Learning Pipeline for Robust Hierarchically Evaluated Enzyme Function Prediction.
papers.abstract: Accurate enzyme annotation remains a major bottleneck in translating rapidly growing protein sequence data into biological knowledge. Enzyme Commission (EC) prediction is particularly challenging because enzyme functions are organized hierarchically, annotations are often imbalanced across classes, and sequence similarity alone may be insufficient to resolve functional differences. To address these challenges, we developed ESM-ECForest, a 2-stage framework that combines protein embeddings generated by the pretrained language model ESM-2 (Evolutionary Scale Modeling 2) with random forest classi
papers.summary: The authors present ESM-ECForest, a two-stage machine learning pipeline that uses protein language model embeddings (ESM-2) combined with random forest classifiers to predict Enzyme Commission (EC) numbers. The approach explicitly accounts for the hierarchical organization of enzyme function and class imbalance, aiming to improve on sequence-similarity-based annotation. The work addresses the growing gap between sequenced proteins and reliable functional annotation.

papers.title: Microbiome-driven precision psychiatry: integrating multi-omics, artificial intelligence, and personalized interventions along the gut-brain axis.
papers.abstract: This scoping review maps evidence for microbiome-driven precision psychiatry in depression and anxiety.
papers.summary: This scoping review maps the evidence for using gut microbiome data to guide personalized treatment of depression and anxiety. It examines how multi-omics data, artificial intelligence, and microbiome-targeted interventions (such as probiotics or diet) could be integrated along the gut-brain axis to enable precision psychiatry. The review likely identifies current gaps and proposes a framework for future research and clinical translation.

papers.title: Gut mycobiome dysbiosis in inflammatory bowel disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: The intestinal mycobiome is increasingly recognized as an important component of host-microbiota interactions in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), yet its contribution to intestinal immune dysregulation remains incompletely characterized. We aimed to characterize alterations in the intestinal mycobiome in patients with inflammatory bowel disease, including Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis, compared with individuals without IBD, focusing on fungal diversity, taxonomic composition, and relative abundance, as well as their potential associations with disease phenotype and inflammatory activ
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis pools existing studies to characterize how the gut fungal community (mycobiome) differs in people with inflammatory bowel disease compared with healthy controls. It focuses on fungal diversity, taxonomic composition, and relative abundance, and explores links to disease type and inflammatory activity. The work consolidates evidence that IBD is associated with mycobiome dysbiosis, though the abstract does not report specific effect sizes.

papers.title: Phenotypic and genomic characterization of a halophilic sulfate-reducing bacterium Desulfoplanes aerotolerans sp. nov. from a petroleum reservoir and its possible implication in pipeline corrosion.
papers.abstract: The issue of biogenic corrosion of steel equipment is especially pressing for petroleum reservoirs with high-salinity formation water containing sulfate. The predominance of sulfate-reducing bacteria of the genus Desulfoplanes in formation water samples from petroleum reservoirs in Tatarstan (Russia) was previously demonstrated using 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing and metagenomic analysis. The present study is devoted to the isolation, phenotypic and genomic characterization of the sulfate-reducing bacterial strain Desulfoplanes sp. PS50T and its involvement in steel corrosion. Studying the
papers.summary: The authors isolated and characterized a new halophilic sulfate-reducing bacterium, Desulfoplanes aerotolerans sp. nov. strain PS50T, from a petroleum reservoir in Tatarstan, Russia. Phenotypic and genomic analyses describe its salt tolerance and ability to grow in the presence of oxygen, and the study links the organism to steel corrosion in oilfield pipelines. The work connects prior 16S rRNA and metagenomic detection of Desulfoplanes in formation water to a cultured representative relevant to microbially influenced corrosion.

papers.title: Gut microbiome taxonomic and functional capacity alterations in CHD and HFpEF.
papers.abstract: The gut microbiome is known to modulate metabolic health, yet its role in coronary heart disease (CHD) and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) remains unclear. In the present study, we profiled the gut microbiome of 234 participants using shotgun metagenomic sequencing across controls (n = 43), individuals with low-risk atherosclerosis (LRAS, n = 23), and patients with CHD + HFpEF (n = 168). Species richness was significantly increased in CHD + HFpEF, with no disruption in taxonomic evenness. LRAS did not diverge significantly in alpha metrics. In contrast, beta diversity an
papers.summary: Shotgun metagenomic profiling of 234 participants found that patients with combined coronary heart disease and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (CHD+HFpEF) had significantly higher gut microbiome species richness than controls, without loss of taxonomic evenness, while low-risk atherosclerosis showed no significant alpha-diversity shift. Beta diversity and functional capacity differences distinguished the disease group, suggesting disease-associated microbiome restructuring rather than simple dysbiosis-driven diversity loss.

papers.title: Cerebrospinal fluid metagenomic next-generation sequencing for culture-negative anaerobic central nervous system infection involving Prevotella oris: attribution challenges in low-biomass specimens.
papers.abstract: Anaerobic central nervous system (CNS) infections are uncommon but diagnostically difficult because fastidious organisms may be suppressed by empirical antimicrobial therapy and conventional cultures may remain negative. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) can recover microbial nucleic acids in this setting, but low microbial biomass creates a central attribution problem: a detected organism may represent active infection, introduced commensal DNA, laboratory background, or bioinformatic misclassification. This narrative Mini Review uses Prevotella oris as a
papers.summary: This mini-review examines the diagnostic challenges of using cerebrospinal fluid metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) to identify anaerobic CNS infections, using Prevotella oris as a case example. The authors highlight that low microbial biomass in CSF makes it difficult to determine whether a detected organism reflects true infection, contaminating commensal DNA, laboratory background, or bioinformatic misclassification. The work emphasizes the need for careful interpretation frameworks when applying mNGS to culture-negative anaerobic CNS infections.

papers.title: Dietary exogenous microRNAs in the gut: biological effects, mechanistic evidence, and controversies.
papers.abstract: Dietary exogenous microRNAs (miRNAs) have emerged as potential mediators of interorganismal communication, with growing interest in their ability to influence gastrointestinal physiology and the gut microbiota. These molecules encompass plant-derived miRNAs implicated in cross-kingdom regulation, animal-derived dietary miRNAs involved in cross-species communication, and maternal milk miRNAs that may participate in mother-to-offspring molecular crosstalk. A proportion of dietary miRNAs are associated with extracellular vesicles or other protective complexes, which may enhance their stability du
papers.summary: This review examines dietary microRNAs from plants, animals, and milk that may survive digestion and influence gut physiology and the microbiome. It discusses evidence for cross-kingdom and cross-species communication, the protective role of extracellular vesicles, and ongoing controversies about whether these effects are biologically meaningful.

papers.title: Building biologically relevant in vitro models of the human gut microbiota: methodological considerations, current challenges, and future perspectives.
papers.abstract: The human gut microbiota (HGM) plays a pivotal role in human health by regulating metabolic, immune, and neurological processes and contributes to the susceptibility to various diseases. The increasing interest in microbiota-targeted therapies has highlighted the need for in vitro models capable of accurately reproducing the composition, function, and ecological dynamics of the intestinal microbial ecosystem. This review examines the methodological factors that determine the biological relevance of HGM in vitro models, emphasizing that reliable experimental outcomes depend not only on the choi
papers.summary: This review examines the methodological factors that determine how biologically relevant in vitro models of the human gut microbiota are, arguing that reliable results depend on more than just the choice of model system. It covers current challenges in reproducing the composition, function, and ecological dynamics of the intestinal microbial ecosystem and outlines future perspectives for microbiota-targeted research.

papers.title: Interpretable detection-based image classification for differential diagnosis of vaginal discharge using smartphone-assisted microscopy.
papers.abstract: The vaginal discharge is a common clinical presentation associated with diverse infectious and microbiota-related conditions. Existing artificial intelligence (AI)-based diagnostic approaches have predominantly focused on detection of individual pathogens and have rarely integrated microbiota-associated conditions within a diagnostic framework. We developed an explainable deep learning framework for automated analysis of Gram-stained vaginal smear images acquired using handheld smartphones or tablets positioned over a conventional light microscope eyepiece.
papers.summary: The authors developed an explainable deep learning framework that analyzes Gram-stained vaginal smear images captured through a smartphone or tablet mounted on a conventional light microscope. Unlike prior AI approaches focused on detecting individual pathogens, this framework integrates microbiota-associated conditions into a differential diagnosis of vaginal discharge. The work demonstrates that smartphone-assisted microscopy combined with interpretable AI can support clinical diagnosis in resource-limited settings.

papers.title: Gut microbiome and gut-derived metabolites to identify the transition from metabolically healthy to unhealthy obesity: a mini review.
papers.abstract: Obesity is a metabolically heterogeneous condition with distinct metabolic phenotypes, ranging from metabolically healthy obesity (MHO) to metabolically unhealthy obesity (MUO). Although individuals with MHO initially lack cardiometabolic dysfunction, many transition to MUO over time, exponentially increasing their risk for type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease. In this mini-review, we synthesize recent evidence from multi-omic cohort studies evaluating gut microbiome composition and gut-derived metabolites as functional biomarkers of obesity heterogeneity and drivers of metabolic decline
papers.summary: This mini-review synthesizes evidence from multi-omic cohort studies on how gut microbiome composition and gut-derived metabolites may serve as biomarkers distinguishing metabolically healthy obesity (MHO) from metabolically unhealthy obesity (MUO), and as potential drivers of the transition between these states. The authors argue that microbiome and metabolite profiles could help identify individuals at risk of progressing to MUO, which carries elevated risk of type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease.

papers.title: Investigating the Effect of Oral Probiotic Capsules on Postpartum Sleep Quality in Primiparous Women: A triple-blind randomised controlled trial.
papers.abstract: Quality of sleep is an important indicator of health. Sleep disturbance and daytime fatigue is one of the most common problems in the postpartum period. Early postpartum (first 4 weeks) is when sleep is most disturbed. The gut microbiota may affect sleep quality and affect host health through the production of metabolites and compounds. This study aimed to determine the effect of oral probiotic capsule on the quality of sleep after delivery in primiparous women.
papers.summary: This triple-blind randomized controlled trial tested whether oral probiotic capsules improve sleep quality in first-time mothers during the early postpartum period, when sleep disturbance is most common. The rationale is that gut microbiota may influence sleep via metabolite production. The abstract does not report results, so the key finding cannot yet be assessed.

papers.title: Evaluating traditional Chinese medicine modulation of the gut microbiota-bile acid axis in metabolic and inflammatory diseases: mechanistic evidence and translational priorities.
papers.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), obesity, type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2D), and inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) are clinically distinct disorders that share perturbations in intestinal ecology, bile-acid composition, epithelial barrier function, and immune-metabolic regulation. Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) may modify these interconnected processes, but the translational significance of reported effects remains uncertain. Changes in microbial composition are often interpreted as mechanisms without evidence of altered microbial function, bile-acid profiles o
papers.summary: This review examines how traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) may influence metabolic and inflammatory diseases (MASLD, obesity, T2D, IBD) through the gut microbiota–bile acid axis. The authors argue that many reported microbial shifts are over-interpreted as mechanisms without functional or bile-acid evidence, and they outline translational priorities to strengthen causal inference. The paper is a critical synthesis rather than new primary data.
